sentences.text: Protitanichthys is an extinct genus of large arthrodire placoderms belonging to the family Coccosteidae.
Although it resembles other coccosteids, this animal possessed a proportionally narrower skull and smaller eye orbits.
It ranks as the second-largest known coccosteid, surpassed only by the genus Livosteus.
Most known specimens measure about 0.5 meters long, though rare fossils exceed 2 meters.
The type species was originally described based on a cranial roof approximately 20 cm long found in Ohio.
The genus Protitanichthys was first described by Eastman in 1907.
Many fragmented remains of the species Protitanichthys rockportensis have been found in Michigan.
Protitanichthys belongs to the family Coccosteidae and the clade Coccosteomorphi within Eubrachythoraci.
It is classified in the class Placodermi.
The Paleobi Database classifies Protitanichthys as a member of the family Panxiosteidae.
Protitanichthys lived between 393.47 and 382.31 million years ago.
This corresponds to the Middle Devonian, specifically from the Eifelian to the Lower Givetian stages.
Fossils of this animal are found in the Delaware Limestone of Ohio and the Rockport Quarry Limestone of Michigan.
It is debated whether Protitanichthys rockportensis is a distinct species from P. fossatus, as differences are limited to time and location.
